raw.details:
Note: Every individual participant must also hold a valid Platinum Pass / General Event Pass to be eligible for entry and participation.

  • Candidates are required to go throught COC (Code of Conduct) to ensure you have a thorough understandings of the event . It covers almost all the queries that participants may have.
  • Candidates are advised to get yourselves familiar with https://meet.jit.si/ as it will be used for monitoring purposes with all candidates required to be on meeting during the complete event.

About the Opportunity:

Cliffesto ’26 Hackathon is a 12-hour offline web development hackathon where participants will work in teams to build a fully functional website based on a problem statement provided at the beginning of the event.

The hackathon provides participants with an opportunity to develop their web development, problem-solving, UI/UX, teamwork and presentation skills while working under a time-bound challenge.

Event Details:

  • Event: Hackathon
  • Duration: 12 Hours
  • Mode: Offline
  • Team Size: 2–5 Members
  • Eligibility: Open to all students

Problem Statement:

The problem statement will be disclosed at the start of the hackathon.

Teams are required to develop a solution that follows the requirements and constraints specified in the problem statement.

Development Guidelines:

  • The final solution must be a fully functional website.
  • Teams may use programming languages, frameworks and tools of their choice, subject to the event rules and problem statement.
  • All development and presentation work must be completed within the 12-hour timeframe.
  • The submitted solution must be original and developed during the hackathon.

Submission Requirements:

Each team must submit:

  • Project code
  • Deployment link, if applicable
  • Final presentation

The project code must be uploaded to a GitHub repository, with access provided to the judging panel.

Teams qualifying through the Preliminary Round will present their solutions to the judges in their respective time slots on the following day.

Judging Criteria:

The submissions will be evaluated on the following parameters:

  • Functionality – 40%
       The website should be fully functional and aligned with the problem statement.
  • Innovation – 20%

           Creative and unique approaches to solving the given problem.

  • UI/UX Design – 20%
       User-friendly and visually appealing interface.
  • Code Quality – 10%
       Clean, well-structured and documented code.
  • Presentation – 10%
       Clear and concise explanation of the proposed solution during the final presentation.

Rounds:

The hackathon will consist of two rounds:

  • Preliminary Round
  • Final Round

A maximum of 7 teams will qualify for the Final Round.

Important Rules:

  • Teams must arrive at the venue 30 minutes before the start of the hackathon.
  • The use of pre-built templates or code is strictly prohibited unless explicitly allowed by the organisers.
  • AI chatbots such as ChatGPT may be used only for assistance purposes.
  • Automated AI agents, autonomous systems, IDE-integrated AI chatbots, or applications/AI tools capable of generating complete code are restricted during the hackathon. Violation may result in disqualification.
  • Internet access will be provided at the venue.
  • Plagiarism, copying solutions from others, hacking or other unethical practices may result in immediate disqualification.
  • All submissions must be original and developed during the hackathon.
  • Participants are encouraged to bring their own laptops, chargers and other necessary equipment.
  • Basic amenities, including Wi-Fi and power outlets, will be provided.

Eligibility & Team Requirements:

  • The hackathon is open to all students.
  • Each team must consist of 2 to 5 members.
  • All members of a team must be from the same institute.
  • Each team must provide a valid team name and contact details of a team captain who will serve as the primary point of contact.
  • All participants must carry valid identification proof (Preferable Student ID card).

AN IMPORTANT NOTE:

  • The organizers reserve the right to modify the rules or guidelines at any time. Any such changes will be communicated to the participants promptly.
  • Decisions made by the judging panel will be final and binding on all teams. No appeals or queries regarding the judgment will be entertained.
  • Prize pool is subjected to the number of participants and on the discretion of the organising committee.
  • In case of any dispute, ambiguity, or matter concerning the interpretation or implementation of these guidelines or any aspect of the event, from commencement through prize distribution, the Event Head shall have the final authority to make the decision. Such decision shall be final and binding on all participating teams and participants, and no appeal or further dispute shall be entertained. 
  • Teams are responsible for ensuring their submission complies with the guidelines.
  • Cliffesto'26 reserves the right to disqualify any team at any stage for non-compliance with the rules or misconduct.
  • For any queries or clarifications, participants are encouraged to contact the Cliffesto'26 organizing team.

*Guidelines are indicative and can be changed by organising committee. The final guidelines and instructions will be communicated by the Event Head and organizing team on the day of the event.

*Prize pool is subject to the number of participants received and may be revised accordingly.
